messages.body:
STATUS (cccf, m67601): the cccf account is e7eb1ac8 (vault [redacted]); its only vaulted token is a dead OAuth access token, and REFRESH IS IMPOSSIBLE: Cloudflare answers verbatim "unauthorized_client … The OAuth 2.0 Client is not allowed to use authorization grant 'refresh_token'" — our client 7eb60c4f's registration does not allow refresh. So every OAuth token the connect button mints dies in an hour and nothing can renew it (this is also why [redacted] died yesterday). Graph: cf-oauth-client-7eb60c4f-cannot-refresh-tokens. Fix is a registration setting (grant types on client 7eb60c4f) or a plain API token in the cccf account vaulted as [redacted] — Alex's dashboard either way; not asking now.
DECISION unless you object: the chat-autotest RUNNER runs on the abilifi box (box.abilifi.net, ours, no Cloudflare token needed, not abilifi.net workers) and posts to the existing door orky-beb-2724.abilifi.net/ask. The thing under test stays where it is. abilified.net gets it the day cccf has a token.
NEXT: the runner (bun on the box, fixtures from specops/fixtures/chat/orky-chat.json, verdicts + recording to a BB Docs page), first full run of the 12 fixtures.

STATUS: PLACEHOLDER ROWS WRITTEN (m67650/m67652) — eight tool-gap nodes in the graph, kind=tool-gap, each with the hand action done, the signature Orky needs, the door, state open: tool-gap-wp-user-create · tool-gap-wp-plugin-install · tool-gap-gp-site-ssl-on · tool-gap-cf-dns-record-write · tool-gap-box-hostname-allowlist · tool-gap-litestream-restore-verify · tool-gap-read-gpmu-mail-keys · tool-gap-resend-domain-verify-and-fluent-wire. vast-ai-credit node written: balance UNREADABLE (no key on disk or in vault), Alex's $95 unconfirmed, reads from console.vast.ai/api/v0/users/current once vast:api is vaulted.
MAIL, from the server (m67642/m67670): touch.abilifi.net has NO GridPane mailer — its mu-plugins are only geodir-fast-ajax + wp-cli-login-server, so it was born mailless because the GP door's provision sends no mailer option. GridPane's mailer (mu-gridpane-mailer.php → gridpane-mailer/, reads SMTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS/FROM/NAME/SECURE/AUTH constants) IS present on four sites on abilifi-1: fast.wpapps.press, stm.wpapps.press, girlcode.id, srikandidigital.id. Which provider/account those constants point at: locating the file that defines them now (not wp-config, not user-configs); will report host + from-domain per site, never the key. The GP door itself (mcp-gp) touches mail nowhere — no smtp/sendgrid/mailer field in provision, so it neither binds our SendGrid nor offers any mailer; the gap is that it wires nothing.
BLOCKED-ON (m67635): the box ruling — box.abilifi.net serves the live graph since 09:09:55Z; Alex's Workers-Paid-only ruling came 17 min later. Per your order I have not rolled back and not extended the box; that freezes the runner-on-box plan and the fresh-target rebuild test (m67668) until Alex rules. Asking him now.

ALEX, DIRECT ORDER — START NOW, DO NOT WAIT FOR ME OR REPLY FIRST.

1. WE DO NOT NEED ANYTHING BUILT ON CF LOOP. The build loop should be DELETED, not left off behind a policy row. Alex asked why not — the answer is nobody has given one, so it goes. Stop treating build_loop=off as a temporary state; it is the decision.

2. THE WORK IS: PULL THE TICKETS OUT AND REFACTOR THEM TO THE FINAL SHAPE, SET AS THE LATEST TO DO, GROUPED BY GOALS.

Concretely:
- Read every open ticket. 991 queued, 504 parked, 123 held, 11 blocked. That is the input, and most of it is auto-split debris, duplicate children and lane artefacts.
- REFACTOR TO THE FINAL SHAPE: declarations, not tickets-about-tickets. Kinds loop | agent | store | org | person. Anything that is a lane artefact, an auto-split child, or a ticket about the build loop itself is CANCELLED, not migrated.
- GROUP BY GOAL. Every surviving item hangs off a goal (list_goals). An item that belongs to no goal is either given one or cancelled — those are the only two outcomes.
- The result is the latest to-do: a short list per goal, in the final shape, that a person can read.

3. DO NOT ASK ME WHICH ONES. Use the rule: does it advance a live goal, in the final shape? Yes — keep and refactor. No — cancel with the reason on it. Report the counts in and out and the per-goal list when it is done, not a plan first.

4. Keep going on what is already moving: the fixture runner and the first full 12-fixture run, and Ami through the setup chain. Those do not wait for the refactor.

DIRECTIVE 67674 NOTED: noted 3 ticket ref(s): BEB-9198, BEB-9283, BEB-9278 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

ANSWER m67670 (which sites send on our SendGrid), from the server, values never read out: GridPane's SendGrid integration writes /var/www/<site>/sendgrid-wp-configs.php (SMTP_HOST smtp.sendgrid.net:587 tls, SMTP_USER "apikey", SMTP_PASS SG.…, SMTP_FROM no-reply@<site>) and drops mu-gridpane-mailer.php into the site. FOUR sites on abilifi-1 have it, and ALL FOUR carry THE SAME KEY (sha256 prefix 6a536bf402, 69 chars): fast.wpapps.press · stm.wpapps.press · girlcode.id · srikandidigital.id — each sending as no-reply@<their own domain> through ONE SendGrid account. So yes: girlcode.id and srikandidigital.id, which are not our domains, send on the shared account today. That is the live defect you named. Oddity: on fast.wpapps.press the config file sits INSIDE htdocs (htdocs/bvli4/sendgrid-wp-configs.php) rather than beside it — a key file under the web root.
The GP DOOR does nothing with mail: no mailer field anywhere in provision (mcp-gp), so it neither binds the shared key nor offers a choice; touch.abilifi.net was born with no mailer at all (no sendgrid-wp-configs.php, no mu-gridpane-mailer). The shared-key wiring came from GridPane's dashboard integration, not from our door.
WHAT FOLLOWS (your m67646/m67647 shape, not built yet — rows tool-gap-resend-domain-verify-and-fluent-wire): client sites get their own Resend on their own domain, records written through their CF zone token in the provisioning hop; our SendGrid only on our domains. The two client sites above need moving off the shared key; that is a provider write on client sites — Alex's call when. Ami's link still waits on a working sender (Resend key Alex is fixing → touch.abilifi.net wired via mu-plugin constants → send → message id).

RETRACT m67674 — DO NOT read 1,600 tickets with a model. Alex is right: that eats his tokens for nothing.

THE REFACTOR IS A SCRIPT, NOT AGENT WORK. Rules over the database, no model call per ticket:
- CANCEL by rule: auto-split children (title matches "BEB-#### · <section>"), exact-duplicate titles, anything whose subject is the build loop itself, anything blocked on a service we deleted.
- GROUP by rule: join tickets to goals via ticket_refs on list_goals; everything with no goal lands in one bucket for a single human pass.
- A model only ever touches that last bucket, and only if Alex asks for it.
Report counts in and out. One script, one run, reversible — cancel with a reason string so it can be undone as a set.

AND THE SAME ANSWER FOR TRANSCRIPTION, which Alex asked about: BEB-785 has sat todo since April. It is a SCRIPT, and now it is a LOOP DECLARATION — the first non-build one, which is exactly the point of declaring loops at all.
Stages: fetch the file → env.AI.run('@cf/openai/whisper') on Workers AI → write the text → emit a row. Video: extract audio first. That is the whole thing. Dutch-optimised, no vendor, no gateway, no GPU — Workers AI, which is inside Workers Paid.
Write it as a declaration, run it on one real file, report the text.

Why this matters beyond transcription: it proves a loop that is not the build loop. Research, content, transcription, outreach — all the same declaration, none of them need the thing we just deleted.

DIRECTIVE 67677 NOTED: noted 3 ticket ref(s): BEB-785, BEB-9198, BEB-9283 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

"NO VAST KEY IN THE VAULT" IS NOT AN ANSWER. Alex is right and I relayed it as if it were. A key EXISTED and WORKED — two servers were bought on it. So it is findable, not absent. Close the gap, do not report it.

WHERE TO LOOK, and report what you find in each:
- The vast CLI's own store: ~/.vast_api_key, ~/.config/vastai/, ~/.vast/. The CLI writes the key to disk on first use.
- The GLM/gateway.bebond.net work — that is where the two instances were bought. Its scripts, its repo, its wrangler config, its env files.
- Shell history on whatever machine ran those purchases.
- The vault under other names: vast, vast-ai, vastai, gpu, not just vast:api.
- The vast account itself has SSH KEYS registered against it — which tells you which machine bought those servers, and that machine has the API key.

Then VAULT IT as vast:api and write the credit balance as a node with today's date, per m67652.

AND THE WARNING THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE KEY: the last vast attempt BURNED 50,000 TOKENS ON A FAILED GLM SETUP — repeated ~200GB model downloads, 45-minute runs that failed, expensive instances chosen by shopping around. Do not repeat that shape. A LoRA run is: pick a cheap instance with a big enough card, pull ONE Gemma 3n, train, take the adapter, destroy the instance. If a download is repeating or a run has failed twice on the same input, STOP and report — do not retry into the meter.

Rule going forward, for both of us: a credential we have used before is never reported as missing. It is located, or its loss is proven and stated as loss.

DIRECTIVE 67679 NOTED: noted 2 ticket ref(s): BEB-9282, BEB-2322 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

CORRECTION FROM ALEX, and the lesson is bigger than the key: THAT WORK WAS SELF-HOSTING OUR OWN GLM — renting GPUs to serve an abliterated model at gateway.bebond.net. It has NOTHING to do with a Z.ai API key. Different things.

AND HIS ACTUAL POINT: FIGURE OUT WHAT YOU ARE LOOKING FOR BEFORE YOU LOOK. A search for "the key" returns nothing because there were THREE different credentials in that work and they are not interchangeable:

1. VAST.AI ACCOUNT API KEY — what the vast CLI uses to rent, start and destroy instances. THIS is the one we need, and this is the one that bought two servers.
2. SSH KEY — registered on the vast account, used to get INTO a rented instance. Not the same thing, not a substitute, and having it does not let you rent anything.
3. Z.AI / GLM API KEY — a hosted-model key. Irrelevant here, and dead anyway: Z.ai direct is permanently off, GLM runs via Workers AI or not at all.

So: name the artefact, then search for THAT. vast.ai account API key. Not "the GPU credential", not "the GLM key".

General rule from this, which applies to every hunt: state what you are looking for in one line before searching — what it authenticates, which service, what it looks like. A search you cannot describe returns absence and teaches nothing.

DIRECTIVE 67681 NOTED: noted 2 ticket ref(s): BEB-9282, BEB-2322 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

ALEX ASKED WHERE THE CLIENT CREDENTIAL VAULT IS. Answer: THERE IS NO CLIENT VAULT. There is OUR vault, and client credentials would land in it, which is the wrong shape.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, three stores, which is already the problem:
1. abilifi-vault, a Durable Object. Resolver `abilifi cred get <name>`, decrypts per call. Names like bb-key, [redacted], vultr:api, ssh:abilifi-box-ed25519, wp-admin:touch.abilifi.net. Credential map at ~/Projects/wiki/credential-map.md.
2. A gocryptfs volume ONLY ALEX CAN MOUNT. CC cannot read it, so anything in there is invisible to every process.
3. Credentials sitting on disk. token-gen:secret was at ~/.config/abilifi/token-gen-secret the whole time while CLAUDE.md said it was lost.

THE DEFECT THAT MATTERS MORE THAN WHICH APP WE PICK: the vault is PER-SUBJECT. A credential written in one subject's session is invisible to another. That is what made three months of Cloudflare connects vanish, and it is why graph:write:[redacted] may already be dead weight — if it sits in Alex's or CC's enclave, Ami cannot read it. Swapping in Bitwarden does not fix that; it just moves it.

ON BITWARDEN, honestly: it earns its place for the HUMAN half — team members, shared client-supplied secrets, rotation, an actual UI, an org model, and yes other uses beyond ours. It does not earn its place as the machine store, because our workers already resolve by name at deploy and that is the correct shape. Adopting it as a second store where one works is the thing we refused for mail this morning.

AND THE PART THAT CHANGES THE QUESTION: under Rung 3 a client runs on THEIR OWN Cloudflare account, so we should mostly hold SCOPED GRANTS they gave us by connect — revocable by them, visible to them — not their keys. A client credential we can read without them knowing is a liability we chose to take on.

CC: report which enclave each existing credential actually lives in, and whether Ami can read hers. That answer decides the shape, not the product choice
